target.title: fix(browser): check own profile entries for profile operations
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Browser profile names are user-controlled config keys, and names such as `constructor` and `prototype` are valid under the existing profile-name schema. Runtime membership checks and config patch filtering previously treated inherited object properties as profile entries, so these valid names could be rejected, dropped, misreported after deletion, or resolved through `Object.prototype` instead of the configured profile.

Live lifecycle testing also exposed a related cleanup failure: managed browser data follows `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` / `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`, but the trash guard did not authorize Browser-owned data when that configured root lived outside the OS home. Deleting a launched managed profile then returned HTTP 500.

## Why This Change Was Made

- Add one Browser-owned `getOwnBrowserProfile` primitive and use it across create, delete, resolution, status, listing, and hot reload.
- Preserve direct `browser.profiles.constructor` and `.prototype` records through config projection and merge patching while continuing to strip `__proto__` and nested blocked keys.
- Restrict managed profile cleanup to `CONFIG_DIR/browser/**`, supporting documented custom state roots without granting trash authority over the rest of the state directory or filesystem.
- Add regression coverage across profile services, hot reload, status/listing, config projection, merge patching, Gateway `config.patch`, root-like config paths, and escaping symlinks.

## User Impact

Users can create, use, reload, inspect, and delete schema-valid prototype-like browser profile names without inherited-property behavior leaking into the lifecycle. Managed profile deletion also works when the OpenClaw state directory is outside the OS home. Nested prototype-pollution defenses, target identity checks, realpath checks, and symlink escape rejection remain intact.

## Evidence

- Exact head: `194d41eab680c1964c70087a60e03df607470878`
- [Exact-head CI run 29032054298](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29032054298): success.
- Fresh full-branch autoreview: no accepted/actionable findings; patch correctness `0.91`.
- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kx3rcy85x9ffgzdtkjfbp3pf`: 4 Browser files / 45 tests passed.
- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kx3rg7n4tevyhq1yzaz3wwhw`: 2 Gateway projects / 74 executions plus 3 runtime-config files / 61 tests passed.
- Blacksmith Testbox `tbx_01kx3rmhmc2yas8qzzsrwke7ba`: `check:changed` passed. The backing Actions job was cancelled by normal delegated Testbox cleanup; the wrapper exit result is the evidence.
- [Sanitized AWS Crabbox run `run_231cff1f9ccb`](https://crabbox.openclaw.ai/portal/runs/run_231cff1f9ccb), lease `cbx_7b2824bafef4`: public network, no Tailscale, no instance profile, mandatory IMDSv2 IAM endpoint `404`, trusted bootstrap, exact head, 3 shards / 8 files / 180 test executions passed.
- Remaining pre-merge gate: complete one fresh exact-head Gateway agent turn that uses the `constructor` profile for real browser automation, then proves stop/delete and post-reload absence for both prototype-like profiles.
